label: January 26–February 01
title: “Teach These Things Freely unto Your Children” —  Genesis 5

items.text: Sin limits our ability to see, feel, and hear the things of God. We must recognize these effects and diligently cultivate attributes that help us overcome them, allowing God to bless us more fully. As we cleanse ourselves, our spiritual senses become sharper.

God calls us to do His work despite our weaknesses. Even prophets like Enoch felt overwhelmed, but the Lord provided courage and support, empowering them to fulfill His divine purposes. We too can find strength in His promises and His help.

The gospel of Jesus Christ, including faith, repentance, baptism, and receiving the Holy Ghost, was taught from the very beginning. This doctrine, like the priesthood, is eternal and essential for our redemption and to be born again.

When we feel inadequate for God's callings, we can learn from prophets who felt similarly. The Savior helps us when He asks us to do hard things. We can approach these challenges with faith in Him, relying on His strength.

To walk with the Savior means to accept His invitation to follow Him. It involves striving to live His teachings and drawing closer to Him daily. This commitment allows us to experience His companionship and guidance throughout our lives.

The Lord's message at Adam’s baptism taught us what we must know and do to be redeemed. Baptism is like being 'born again,' a process we can continue throughout our lives to remain clean and spiritually renewed through Christ.

Scriptural symbols enrich our understanding of Jesus Christ and His doctrine. We can find profound spiritual truths by looking for the symbolism of hearts, ears, eyes, clay, and water within the scriptures, as revealed in Moses 6.

Parents have a sacred duty to teach their children the ways of God, including faith in Jesus Christ, repentance, baptism, and receiving the Holy Ghost. This foundational doctrine guides families toward righteousness and eternal blessings.

Enoch’s story reveals his humility, God’s recognition of his potential, and the great work he performed as a prophet. Despite his insecurities, he became a powerful instrument in God's hands, demonstrating what is possible with divine help.

The doctrine of salvation, including faith in the Savior, repentance, baptism, and the gift of the Holy Ghost, has been part of God’s plan from the beginning and will continue until the end of the world. It is the eternal path to redemption.
